tasks.notes:
Evidence surfaced 2026-08-09 during PR #53 review (roadmap 2GN.99's `oxidisation: -1` sentinel fix): `computeLayerGrade` (`engine/generation/decoration.ts`) computes a finite difficulty for ANY technique/material pairing, including ones the technique's own `substrate` test already declares impossible, because per-component substrate enforcement (this task) does not exist yet. Measured exhaustively across all 16 techniques × 16 materials: 49 gate-failing pairings across 9 material-gated techniques are still gradeable. Six invert — a gate-failing material grades EASIER than every legitimate substrate, at craft 0.8: `glaze` (gate: non-combustible ceramic) — linen 0.7873, leather, ash all grade above fired-clay's 0.7707, the one material that actually passes; `overlay` (gate: rigid surface) — linen 0.7947, leather grade above ash's 0.7680; `gilding` (gate: sufficiently rigid surface) — linen 0.7627 grades above leather's 0.7560. The `glaze` case is sharpest: its gate reads `combustibility <= 2`, but its `TECHNIQUE_MATERIAL_SENSITIVITY` row weights only `fragility`/`porosity` — nothing that knows a material would burn in the kiln — so linen, which would literally combust, currently reads as the easiest material in the catalogue to glaze.

Two alternative fixes considered and rejected in the PR #53 round: (1) making `computeLayerGrade` substrate-aware directly — correct, but a real behavioural change across every technique that would move many pinned calibration figures, and it is this task's own scope, not a side-fix; (2) authoring more `-1` not-applicable sentinels onto `combustibility`/`rigidity` to mirror `oxidisation` — rejected because those are honest continuous scales (`rigidity: 1` carries real meaning elsewhere, e.g. why linen drapes), so the mismatch is not in the material data. tasks.description: `tests/fixtures/world.ts` + `src/lib/data/classification.ts` + `src/lib/types/artefact.ts` — geological fixture correction and whole-rule-set tag-contribution rebalance
tasks.notes:
`mockGeologicalContext` models only 4 of 16 catalogue materials (bronze/iron/gold/flint), so the other twelve fell through `isAvailable`'s "unmodelled → obtainable" lenience at full weight — measuring 1200 pipeline artefacts found silver the second most common material at 10.3% of components and jade 6.6%, while genuinely-scarce gold sat at 1.4%, giving 53.4% of artefacts at least one "precious" component. Landed (interviewed decision-by-decision per the classification-branch oversight preference; doc 12 §2.25 records the session) as **six named regional worlds** rather than the single `mockFullGeologicalContext` originally scoped — `riverValley`, `highlandMine`, `coastalPort`, `forestInterior`, `desertMargin`, `steppeMargin`, each modelling all 16 materials explicitly and paired with its own `MaterialFlow[]`, so a threshold tuned against one geology is exposed by another. Between them they cover every `AvailabilityLevel` and both exclusion paths (`absent` in `desertMargin`; trade-only-with-no-matching-flow in `forestInterior`, which carries an empty flow array). `mockGeologicalContext` is deliberately left untouched — it is now the fixture that covers the unmodelled-lenience path the six full worlds no longer reach. `sampleWorld()` takes a region argument (default `coastalPort` at the time — superseded by 2GN.88, which dropped the default entirely) and all five samplers gained `--world`, a scope expansion agreed at interview beyond the task's original two files.

**The fixture fix corrected materials but not `elite`, which was the substantive finding.** Re-measuring 7200 artefacts across the six worlds: precious-bearing artefacts fell 55.3% → 27.1%, silver 11.1% → 3.9%, jade 6.6% → 1.4%, and gold rose above jade — the ordering is now archaeologically sane. But `elite` was unmoved (89.8% presence, 35.4% leader) and near-identical in all six worlds (89.2–90.8%) despite radically different material availability, proving it was never material-driven. Investigation found the applied-element rule's 84.6% firing is **structural, not a mistuned threshold**: `expandDecoration` gives each BNF category its own per-component slot rolls (0.45 base chance at the fixture phase), so a ~4.15-component artefact reaches ~87% by arithmetic alone — no weight on a boolean fixes that.

**Two rules retuned**, both for intent-behaviour divergence (the criterion agreed at interview; a rule firing often because the structure is genuinely common is honest and was left alone): R31 now reads a new `ExtractedFeatures.appliedElementCount` at its measured p75 (`>= 4`, firing 25.2%, within a point of retuned R30's 25.3%) instead of the saturating boolean — an extraction-side change agreed at interview, so this task was not data-only; R29 raised to `attachmentDiversity >= 3` (44.4% → 22.3%) with its `partCount >= 3` clause **dropped as inert** (measured identical fire rate with the clause, without it, and with it raised to `>= 4`). R32's 98% firing was investigated and deliberately left: it does not diverge from its stated intent, doc 12 §2.24 had already ruled the same way, and `ornament`'s leadership fell 27.0% → 18.8% on the R31 fix alone — the 2GN.79 entry's original diagnosis blaming it is corrected in doc 12 §2.25. Result: `elite` leadership 35.4% → 27.4%, top four tags now within 12 points rather than 25.

**Durability tested, and one axis failed.** Thresholds are robust to catalogue growth (measured identical at 2×, 4× and 10× the applied-element technique pool — slot count sets the number, pool size only decides which technique fills a slot) and to geology (22–26% across the six worlds). They are **not** robust to phase attributes: R31 fires 4.3% at `decorativeEmphasis` 0.1 and 48.1% at 1.0; 2.3% at `craftSpecialisation` 0.1 and 74.5% at 1.0. That affects every measured threshold in the file including §2.24's seven, and spawned spike 2GN.80 plus recalibration tasks 2GN.82–85. Also spawned 2GN.81 (Rule Calibration Explorer panel) and fixed five pre-existing broken `assignMaterial`/`expandDecoration` call sites in the samplers (argument order; `deno check` was failing on `scripts/dev/` and two samplers threw at runtime). New coverage: `tests/fixtures/world.test.ts` (11 tests), `src/lib/data/calibration.test.ts` (fire-rate regression guard over all 43 rules — the gap that let R31 sit at 85% since 2GN.34), plus extraction and rule tests for the new field.

tasks.description: design spike — does a material's classificatory value derive from static catalogue tags (`precious-metal`/`precious-stone`) or from its situation in the generated world?
tasks.notes:
Ruled 2026-08-04, jointly with 2GN.80 — see doc 11 §2.9 (decision) and doc 12 §2.28 (rationale + measurements). **Status tags are culture-relative; physical/function tags stay absolute, and the boundary is cut by the tag a rule awards rather than the feature its condition reads** — which catches R12/R15, whose conditions are physical but whose awards are status claims, alongside the eleven decoration-conditioned rules. Baselines are sampled empirically per culture-phase at world generation (pipeline stages 1–7 only, so there is no bootstrap circularity) and cached in world state. Sample size n=400, measured rather than inherited: doc 12 §2.27's n=100 knee was for fire rates (a proportion), while a baseline is a percentile, whose worst-case relative spread runs 20–28% at n=100 and 8–17% at n=400. Percentiles are stored as fractional thresholds because `appliedElementCount` takes only 9–16 distinct integer values and its nearest-rank p90 flips between adjacent integers at any sample size. `PhaseCharacteristics.society.stratification` becomes a live input, gating how much `elite` can exist at all. Drift is recorded against the immediately preceding phase only (magnitude + direction); the proposed culture-wide baseline was dropped as incoherent — it would score an artefact against phases that had not yet happened. `ClassificationRule.condition` widens to `(features, context) => boolean`, amending doc 12 §2.20's pure-function contract. Surfaced 3WS.21 (phase-attribute continuity), on which the drift measure depends.

Original framing: The static model bakes an Earth judgement into `data/materials.ts`: a generated culture with abundant gold would have `elite` stamped across most of its material record under a naive material→tag rule — the tag system reporting a society composed entirely of elites — while obsidian in a culture with no volcanic geology reads ordinary despite being genuinely scarce there. The world-relative alternative derives value from `GeologicalContext.materialAvailability` × `CulturalProfile.materialAffinities` × `MaterialAssignment.provenance.source` × `PhaseCharacteristics.society.stratification` (the last currently read by nothing, despite doc 05 §3.2 commenting "Affects elite/utilitarian distribution"). Deliverables: decision recorded in doc 11 (locked decisions) and doc 12 (propagation register); the derived-value formula if world-relative wins; a ruling on whether `MaterialTag`'s `precious-*` members survive as classification inputs; and the resulting contract for whether `extractFeatures` needs world context, which determines whether doc 12 §2.20's pure-function contract breaks. Surfaced 2026-07-31 during 2GN.27 planning, before any material→tag rule was authored.

design spike — are status tags absolute across the world, or relative to the producing culture's norms?
tasks.notes:
Ruled 2026-08-04, jointly with 2GN.77 — see doc 11 §2.9 (decision) and doc 12 §2.28 (rationale + measurements). **Status tags are culture-relative; physical/function tags stay absolute, and the boundary is cut by the tag a rule awards rather than the feature its condition reads** — which catches R12/R15, whose conditions are physical but whose awards are status claims, alongside the eleven decoration-conditioned rules. Baselines are sampled empirically per culture-phase at world generation (pipeline stages 1–7 only, so there is no bootstrap circularity) and cached in world state. Sample size n=400, measured rather than inherited: doc 12 §2.27's n=100 knee was for fire rates (a proportion), while a baseline is a percentile, whose worst-case relative spread runs 20–28% at n=100 and 8–17% at n=400. Percentiles are stored as fractional thresholds because `appliedElementCount` takes only 9–16 distinct integer values and its nearest-rank p90 flips between adjacent integers at any sample size. `PhaseCharacteristics.society.stratification` becomes a live input, gating how much `elite` can exist at all. Drift is recorded against the immediately preceding phase only (magnitude + direction); the proposed culture-wide baseline was dropped as incoherent — it would score an artefact against phases that had not yet happened. `ClassificationRule.condition` widens to `(features, context) => boolean`, amending doc 12 §2.20's pure-function contract. Surfaced 3WS.21 (phase-attribute continuity), on which the drift measure depends.

Original framing: Surfaced 2026-07-31 during 2GN.79's durability testing. Every threshold in `data/classification.ts` is an absolute constant, and every one is strongly phase-sensitive: the retuned applied-element rule fires on 4.3% of output at `decorativeEmphasis` 0.1 and 48.1% at 1.0; 2.3% at `craftSpecialisation` 0.1 and 74.5% at 1.0. So `elite` currently means "unusually decorated *in absolute terms*", which makes a highly decorative culture read as composed almost entirely of elites and an austere one as having none — the same failure 2GN.77 identifies for materials, reached from the decoration side. The alternative derives the threshold from the producing culture's own expected decorative volume, so "lavish" means lavish *for this culture*. ⚠️ `ClassificationRule.condition` currently receives only `ExtractedFeatures` and nothing else (doc 12 §2.20's pure-function contract), so a culture-relative reading breaks that signature — the ruling's main irreversible consequence. Deliverables: decision recorded in doc 11 (locked decisions) and doc 12 (propagation register); if culture-relative wins, the derivation formula and the new `condition` contract; a ruling on whether `PhaseCharacteristics.society.stratification` (read by nothing today, despite doc 05 §3.2 commenting "Affects elite/utilitarian distribution") becomes an input. Sibling to 2GN.77 — consider ruling on both together, since one asks the same question of materials. The Rule Calibration panel (2GN.81) is the instrument for reasoning about this: switching culture preset shows the swing directly (`elite` leads 35.4% against the flat-0.5 fixtures, 0.4% against the low-decoration Tarpan preset).

tasks.description: recalibrate the measured classification thresholds per the 2GN.80 ruling
tasks.notes:
Migrated exactly nine of the eleven measured thresholds the roadmap line names, not all 34 rules the 2GN.80 ruling's selector catches — doc 12 §2.31 corrects the earlier 34-vs-9 conflation (needing-a-baseline and having-a-numeric-threshold-to-recalibrate are different counts). R29 (attachmentDiversity, p90), R30 (decorativeLayerCount, p75), R31 (appliedElementCount, p75), R35 (hasEdge && decorativeLayerCount, p75), R36 (hasContainer && decorativeLayerCount, p75), R40 (decorativeComplexity, p75), R41 (decorativeComplexity, p95), R42 (decorativePerPart, p75), R43 (techniqueComplexity, p90) all migrated to `ClassificationContext.exceeds`.

**Migrating to a ladder rung is not free arithmetic.** Measured against the real pipeline (18 culture-phase cells, n=400 baselines): a rule's fire rate is not `(1 - percentile) * 100` — coarse features (attachmentDiversity, appliedElementCount) carry heavy tie-mass at the interpolated threshold under `exceeds`'s `>=` convention, a third face of doc 12 §2.28's granularity defect that fractional thresholds alone don't cure. R29 at p75 fires 43.4% (recreating the 44.4% rate 2GN.79 retuned away from); p90 (21.5%) reproduces the rule's actual intent. Two rules' historically-measured percentiles (~p93, and a p90 value used as `>= 8`) had no ladder rung at all, resolved by argument from stated intent rather than nearest-number arithmetic (R41 → p95, not p90, to avoid inflating the top elite tier ~45%). tasks.description: design spike — what does the 2GN.80 ruling mean for the 25 categorical relative-award rules 2GN.82 could not migrate
tasks.notes: Ruled 2026-08-13 — see docs/spikes/2GN.97-categorical-relative-award-rules.md, doc 11 §2.12 and doc 12 §2.44. **The brief's framing was wrong and the ruling rejects it.** 2GN.82 left these rules as 'unmigrated, needing a categorical baseline'; measuring all of them found they are not one problem and most need no baseline at all. Count corrected: **24, not 25** — the roadmap figure predated 2GN.87's deletion of R4. Five groups. **(A1) ~10 rules where morphology determines the tag** — fine unchanged. **(A2→ absorbed) ambiguous morphology**: a central perforation reads spindle-whorl or pendant; ruled NOT a baseline problem (prevalence cannot disambiguate a single artefact) and NOT fixable by weight-splitting, because `classifyArtefact` accumulates additively with no suppression, so 'ambiguous' and 'weakly two things' are indistinguishable downstream. **(B-walls) 2 rules unrelativisable** — `wallThickness` is a three-value roll with no quantity beneath it, so one culture's thick may be thinner than another's thin and no baseline can recover it; filed 2GN.120. **(B-bases) 2 rules under-conditioned** — `baseType` IS a genuine categorical (unlike walls, nothing continuous is crushed) and prevalence would be meaningful, but a base is a relation between the base and what it supports: a pedestal under a statue and one under a hat-stand read oppositely with identical `baseType`. No relativisation fixes an under-conditioned rule. **(C) mass/size** — cheap route, `massBand` derives from a scored distribution. **(D) `precious-materials-in-decoration` is stubbed `false`** and cannot fire — 2GN.78 fallout, a fifth dormant rule; once derived it is culture-relative against regional scarcity per 2GN.77, and reads the keyspace 2GN.110 rules. **The finding that outgrew the brief**: 10 of 24 condition on exactly one property, 7 more on two properties of the same component, and only 1 is genuinely relational. ⚠️ The defect crosses doc 11 §2.9's boundary — `perforation-central-rotation` awards `tool`, an AbsoluteTag, and is under-conditioned identically — so it is a property of how conditions are written, not of which vocabulary they award. Filed 2GN.119, scoped to **all 43 rules**. Also surfaced 2GN.118 (are the primitive value-sets rational) while stress-testing `baseType`.

tasks.notes: Ruled 2026-08-06 (doc 11 §2.10, doc 12 §2.33): `decorationVolume` reads `aesthetics.decorativeEmphasis` alone; a new `DecorativeLayer.grade` field reads `society.craftSpecialisation` scaled by a new authored `TECHNIQUE_DIFFICULTY` rating (`data/decorations.ts`, 16 values reviewed per-item). tasks.description: recalibrate `computeLayerGrade` to read technique difficulty per-material, not technique alone
tasks.notes:
Ruled and shipped 2026-08-07 (doc 12 §2.35). Blocked on a prerequisite that had to be built first: `physicalProperties` could not express material difficulty at all, so **2GN.101** rebuilt it (six orthogonal axes plus keyed `reactivity`) before this task could proceed.

**Ships as an unwired post-pass, and that is the honest scope.** `computeLayerGrade` is called inside `expandDecoration`'s slot loop, where no component has an assigned material — assignments live in a parallel `MaterialAssignment[]` from `assignMaterials`, which no production caller runs first. Threading them in would force all six call sites to reorder, and `assignMaterials` consumes PRNG draws, so it would perturb the decoration draw sequence and move every recorded fire rate for reasons unrelated to grade. New `gradeDecorativeLayers` instead re-grades layers as a separate PRNG-free pass, mirroring `assignDecorativeDetails`' position. `expandDecoration` untouched; its grade is now documented as *provisional*. **Nothing in the sampled path changed at ship time, so no calibration pin moved then** — a stronger inertness checkpoint than 2GN.82/2GN.98's partial ones. **Follow-on defect fixed in the same PR #53 review round, 2026-08-09:** the `oxidisation: -1` not-applicable sentinel reached `effectiveDifficulty`'s weighting unguarded, normalising to ≈-1.29 (outside the documented [-1,+1] band) and landing every inert material's `patina` grade below gold's — inverting the gate/difficulty distinction the sentinel exists to express. tasks.description: rebuild `MaterialDefinition.physicalProperties` as orthogonal authored axes
tasks.notes:
Forced out of 2GN.99 on 2026-08-07 (doc 12 §2.35): that task assumed `physicalProperties` could say something useful about how hard a material is to work, and it could not. `workable: boolean` conflated three separate facts — brittleness (obsidian/flint/glass shatter), pliability (linen/leather deform rather than cut) and grain coarseness (granite cannot hold a fine line however carefully worked). `hardness: 'soft'|'medium'|'hard'` was not merely coarse but actively misused: `relief` and `overlay` both carried substrate comments conceding hardness was "standing in as the nearest proxy" for a fracture property the type lacked.

Six authored axes replace the pair — `hardness` (1-10, pegged to the real Mohs scale so values stay independently checkable), `fragility`, `rigidity`, `grainFineness`, `porosity`, `combustibility` (all 1-7) — plus `reactivity: { oxidisation }`, keyed by reaction type so future chemistry is additive. All 16 materials scored against every axis, item-by-item, each argued from real materials practice.

Two axes were discovered mid-review by techniques that had nothing to key on: `patina` is a chemical process (hence `reactivity`, and hence its substrate was `{kind:'none'}` with the live generator patinating stone and glass), and `painting`/`glaze` both wanted absorbency (hence `porosity`), with `combustibility` following from glaze being a firing process. `oxidisation` carries a `-1` not-applicable sentinel feeding a substrate GATE rather than a difficulty penalty — glass has no oxidation chemistry at all, gold has it and is merely resistant (`0`), and keeping those distinct matters.

Axis independence tested, not assumed: obsidian vs granite (same hardness/rigidity, granite less fragile, yet obsidian takes a far finer edge — only `grainFineness` explains it) and gold vs oak. Both pinned as tests.

Four substrate corrections fell out: `patina` gains the oxidation gate; `glaze` a combustibility ceiling; `relief`/`overlay` retire the self-admitted hardness proxy (relief needing BOTH rigidity and fragility, since fragility alone admitted linen and leather); and **`gilding`'s gate was factually wrong** — it required metal, but real gilding is overwhelmingly on wood and gesso, with gilded leather and ceramic well attested. tasks.description: `engine/generation/grammar.ts` — mass proxy sums component footprints; mass bands rebalanced to measured percentiles
tasks.notes:
Surfaced 2026-08-01 auditing all 43 classification rules at the user's request (the 2GN.79 session had cleared 41 of them in prose without per-rule sign-off). Three rules read `massBand` and all three were misbehaving: R27 (`very-heavy` → communal) fired on 0 of 7200 artefacts, and R25/R26 (heavy edge → labour tool; heavy container → storage) fired on 55.8% of edged and 61.1% of container artefacts while their JSDocs claimed contrasts ("labour, **not** a blade weapon"; "storage jar **rather than** tableware") that only hold for a minority.

**Root cause was the proxy, not the band boundaries.** `deriveDimensions` computed `primaryExtent * secondaryExtent * (1 + 0.1 * (parts - 1))`, and both extents are *maxima* across components. Each component draws its size from a three-value ordinal table (4/14/40, 5/15/45, 3/8/18), so with 2–13 components at least one almost always rolled `large` and both axes pinned to 45cm: **57.4% of a 7200-artefact sample landed on exactly 45×45=2025**, one value holding the majority of output. No choice of boundary can separate a distribution like that — any cut either includes the spike (that band ≥57%) or excludes it (everything below sums to ≤43%). Compounding it, the proxy's reachable maximum was 4658 against a `very-heavy` threshold of 5000, making that band unreachable by arithmetic rather than merely rare. Same saturation-by-maximum failure as `appliedElementPresent` in 2GN.79, in a different guise.

Fixed by summing each component's own major×minor footprint instead: a many-part object is genuinely more massive than a one-part object sharing its largest axis, which a maximum can never express. Distribution went from 21 distinct products (top value 57.4%) to 1810 (top value 1.8%), range 9–4658 → 16–12183. Bands then pinned to measured p15/p45/p80/p95 (233/2033/2892/5007), deliberately tapering rather than equal-sized — most excavated finds are portable, and equal quintiles would have claimed a quarter of all finds are too heavy for one person to lift. Resulting spread: negligible 15.3% · light 29.2% · moderate 35.2% · heavy 15.6% · very-heavy 4.8%.

Downstream: R27 0% → 5.0% (alive for the first time), R25 55.8% → 19.5% of edged, R26 61.1% → 24.8% of containers, R37 1.1% → 1.9% and R39 8.5% → 10.6% (their gated presence flags require `massBand` at most `light`, so more artefacts now qualify as wearable). `portability` also reads mass, so `major-effort` and `team-lift` became reachable. Every other rule unchanged to the decimal. The 2GN.79 calibration guard caught the drift and named both moved rules with their sizes — five recorded rates re-recorded and annotated. Two new grammar tests pin the invariants: mass grows with part count (the old proxy rated one and six large components equal), and no single band may hold a majority of output.

tasks.description: `src/lib/types/description.ts` — add `condition?: VariantCondition` to `DescriptionVariant`; define `VariantCondition` (parameter-value gate + craftDomain/materialId/materialTag material gate)
tasks.notes:
Surfaced 2026-08-05 during 2GN.36/2GN.37 planning; widened 2026-08-05 during 2GN.36 authoring. `DescriptionVariant` addresses variants by `property` id + `register` + `emphasis` only — a variant fires for every value of its parameter, since the value itself only reaches the text via a `#slot#`. Two condition gaps surfaced against this:

1. **Within-parameter value gating.** `elongated.crossSection`'s 'round' and 'rectangular' values don't support the same interpretive reading (a round cross-section is held differently to a rectangular one) — one template stretched across every value of a parameter reads as either shallow or false for some values.

2. **Cross-property/material gating.** A geometric reading can depend on the component's *material*, not just its own parameter — 'taper suits a forceful strike' is false if the material is brittle. This was originally scoped as technical-only (craft process is materially determined at the root: grinding bronze, knapping obsidian, paring oak and throwing clay are different processes), but interpretive claims need the same gate for the same reason — a functional reading is a claim about geometry *given* material, not geometry alone. Originally proposed as a technical-only mechanism; interpretive authoring showed the same condition is required there, so both registers share this one field rather than duplicating the concept.

`VariantCondition` fields are optional and any-of within, AND across fields (`{craftDomain: ['stoneWorking'], materialId: ['obsidian']}` requires both). No predicate functions (unlike `DECORATIVE_TECHNIQUES.substrate.test` in `data/decorations.ts`) — description data may cross the save boundary, so the condition must stay serialisable. Component *shape* deliberately has no field: the `property` id already carries it (`elongated.edge` only fires on an elongated component). Sibling-parameter conditions (e.g. edge=double AND crossSection=diamond on the same component) are deliberately out of scope — cheap to add later as a non-breaking extension, and premature inclusion risks the 2GN.87 failure mode (a plausible-looking conjunction that matches zero generated artefacts, silently). tasks.description: design spike — should the artefact vocabulary express a short-bodied edged tool that is not a formed blade (scraper, chisel, small adze)? Today it cannot: `primaryAxisLength` bands `dimensions.primaryExtent`, a `Math.max` over every component's major axis drawn from the same `SHORT_MEDIUM_LONG_CM` table `bladeLengthBand` reads, so a non-short blade always lifts the artefact's axis above `short` and the blade band can never exceed the axis band. Measured over 8000 artefacts (2GN.87): only 6 of 12 `(axis, blade)` pairs occur, in a strict triangle, and `axis === 'short'` carried `blade === 'short'` in all 84 cases. These are among the commonest real assemblage finds, so the absence is a genuine content gap — but 2GN.87 ruled that the deleted R4 never encoded a decision to model them (it was authored in PR #37 review to plug a truth-table cell, with the scraper/chisel reading attached afterwards), so the question is open rather than inherited. If ruled yes, this spike also rules the mechanism: a shorter `elongated.length` rung below `short` / decoupling `bladeLengthBand` from the shared cm table so it bands the component's own proportion rather than absolute size / changing `deriveDimensions` so `primaryExtent` is not a plain `Math.max` (the 2GN.86 fix applied to a second symptom of the same cause). Each shifts fire rates set-wide and needs a recalibration sweep costed before it is chosen. A spike, not an implementation task — same shape as 2GN.80/2GN.77
tasks.notes: Ruled 2026-08-13 — see docs/spikes/2GN.108-short-bodied-edged-tools.md (full spike), doc 11 §2.11 (locked decision) and doc 12 §2.43 (propagation). **The form is ruled in, on tag-space variety grounds rather than archaeological completeness**: short-bodied edged tools occupy the working/craft/domestic region, so their absence removes one region of the tag space rather than thinning the corpus evenly, leaving edged artefacts skewed to blade-family readings — which propagates into culture tag profiles and surfaces as repetition in the lens, the core mechanic. §2.9's culture-relative baselines cannot compensate, since they sample the same narrowed distribution. **All three candidate mechanisms were rejected as symptom-level.** The real defect is that `bladeLengthBand` bands the wrong quantity: absolute length cannot separate a scraper (edge-dominant, short) from a dagger (edge-dominant, long) from a hafted adze (long body, short edge) — the distinction is the grip-to-edge proportion. Re-based accordingly. **Grip-to-edge needs no role vocabulary**: `attachments` is a populated typed graph and `position` plus per-component extents already exist, so the span is a traversal the three plausibility proxies never used. **Root cause: `position` is documented as an oriented axis but minted as a depth-first traversal index**, so a blade can land at position 0 with its haft after it. Normalisation must orient, by **reversal** rather than rejection — a mirrored artefact carries no information, so rejecting it spends re-expansion budget enforcing probabilistically what construction can guarantee. Deferred: the general working-end definition (2GN.115), which blocks implementation rather than this ruling. Filed: 2GN.115, 2GN.116 (component roles, now blocking 2GN.13/2GN.14), 2GN.117 (implementation). ⚠️ 2GN.109 is live — it was contingent, void only if the form had been ruled out. Recalibration is set-wide and shared with 2GN.67, 2GN.69 and 2GN.109; sequence the sweep once.

design spike — should `CulturalProfile.materialAffinities` support per-material entries alongside per-tag ones? Surfaced by 2GN.78 (doc 11 §2.9, doc 12 §2.40) as an accepted expressive loss: the map is keyed by `MaterialTag`, so with the `precious-*` members retired a culture can say "we prize metal" but no longer "we prize gold specifically". Thalassar's authored `precious-metal: 1.2` was the one live instance across the four Explorer presets and was dropped rather than re-expressed as `metal: 1.2`, which would newly favour bronze and iron that culture was never authored to prefer. Rule whether that granularity is worth carrying — and if so whether it belongs in `materialAffinities` as a second keyspace, or is better derived from the material's situation the way 2GN.77 ruled preciousness itself must be. Note the tension: a per-material affinity entry is a culture-authored judgement about one material, which is legitimate (it is *that culture's* opinion, not Earth's) but sits close enough to the retired tags that the boundary wants stating explicitly
tasks.notes: Ruled 2026-08-13 — see docs/spikes/2GN.110-per-material-affinities.md, doc 11 §2.13 and doc 12 §2.45. **Yes: `materialAffinities` is re-keyed by `MaterialSelector`**, the same tagged union 2GN.112 built for `MaterialFlow`, and for the identical reason — `bone`, `glass` and `leather` each name both a `MaterialTag` and a `MaterialName`, so a bare union cannot distinguish them and precedence would make 3 of 16 materials unselectable by one of their readings. Only half the flow pattern transfers: `includes`/`excludes` exists because membership needs subtraction, and affinities are weights with nothing to subtract. **Resolution is most-specific-wins**: a class entry sets a default, a specific entry is an exception to it — `{tag:'metal'}: 1.5` with `{id:'gold'}: 0.8` reads 'all metals are 1.5, except gold, which is 0.8'. A specific entry with no class entry is well-formed and is what recovers Thalassar's dropped intent exactly (`{id:'gold'}: 1.2, {id:'silver'}: 1.2`, no `metal` entry). **This closes the unruled `max` reduction** flagged in `culturalAffinityWeight`'s JSDoc: per-material entries make the multi-value case arrive via the selector rather than via a multi-tag material, and 2GN.84 already measured max discarding authored values whenever the class tag scored higher (3 of 5 dead), so a specific entry could only ever raise a material, never lower it. Product-of-deviations rejected: 1.5 × 0.8 = 1.2, so a below-neutral authored value yields an above-neutral weight. `materials.ts`'s `culturalAffinityWeight` and `decoration.ts`'s `bestMaterialAffinity` move together. ⚠️ `effectiveOptionWeight` (`grammar.ts`) does NOT participate and this is not an inconsistency to reconcile: it weights grammar options by tag-keyed `culturalModifiers` at stage 4, before materials are assigned at stage 6, so it never sees a material; its `?? 0` default differs deliberately. ⚠️ **The tag-versus-tag tie stays explicitly unruled** — no shipped material carries two class tags, and authoring a rule for a shape that does not exist is the defect 2GN.87 punished. Boundary the brief asked for: a per-material affinity is legitimate because it lives in `CulturalProfile` (that culture's opinion), where the retired `precious-*` tags lived in `MaterialDefinition` (Earth's judgement, applied universally) — the test is where the statement lives, not how specific it is.

tasks.description: design spike — should `MaterialDefinition.physicalProperties` carry per-state values at all, and if so which states? 2GN.102 established a working-state convention for `formability` alone and named the inconsistency in `types/artefact.ts`'s preamble without resolving it (doc 12 §2.38); 2GN.105 was then filed presupposing the answer ("at minimum worked vs finished"). Rule the shape before the re-audit: whether a per-state model is warranted or the six pre-2GN.102 axes should instead be pinned to one documented state, how many states (`worked`/`finished`, or a third for `raw`), whether every axis needs every state or only those where the states genuinely differ, and what that does to the authoring burden across 16 materials × 7 axes. `glass`, `iron`, `fired-clay` and `leather` are the known-affected entries. 2GN.105 re-pointed to depend on this rather than on 2GN.102 directly, so the audit follows the ruling instead of assuming it
tasks.notes: Ruled 2026-08-13 — see docs/spikes/2GN.111-per-state-physical-properties.md, doc 11 §2.14 and doc 12 §2.46. **Per-state on `rigidity` alone** (`{worked, finished}`); every other axis stays scalar with a documented state. Two states, not three. **The consumers are the fault line, not the physics**: three axes vary strongly by state and one marginally, but what decides the shape is which state each reader needs. `relief` (`formability >= 3`) and wire-drawing (`formability >= 5`) ask working-state questions; the three `rigidity >= 3` gates on overlay/studs/gilding ask a finished-state one; `computeLayerGrade` reads its six difficulty axes in the working state, since difficulty is incurred while working. Bronze is the deciding case — whether it can be forged into a raised form and whether the finished object holds applied leaf are both true and are different numbers, so no single convention serves both. Only `rigidity` is asked in both states by different consumers. Pinning: `formability` working (already correct), `fragility` working, `hardness` working, `grainFineness`/`porosity`/`combustibility` state-independent. Blanket per-state rejected — 16×7×3 = 336 values to capture variation in four axes, and a uniform shape invites false precision (an author given three boxes fills all three). `raw` rejected: no consumer asks about an unworked material. ⚠️ **`fragility` and `hardness` are a live defect**: both feed `computeLayerGrade` and nothing else, so working state is the only correct reading, yet both are authored finished-state — glass carries `fragility: 7` (cold) while decorated hot, fired clay `6` (fired) while decorated wet, both inflating difficulty. The correction is independent of the shape change and ⚠️ **shifts `meanDecorativeGrade`** for those materials, so the 2GN.79 guard will flag it — sequence with the other recalibration-bearing work. Rescoped 2GN.105.

tasks.description: design spike — **RULED 2026-08-12 (PR #57 review), implemented same branch.** Should `MaterialFlow.specificMaterials` narrow a flow or widen it? Neither: the field is gone, and `MaterialFlow` now selects via `includes: MaterialSelector[]` plus optional `excludes`, where `MaterialSelector` is `{ tag: MaterialTag } | { id: MaterialName }`. A flow supplies a material when some `includes` selector names it and no `excludes` selector does — union then subtract, no precedence, no ordering. **Why the shape changed rather than the operator:** the old `materialTag` + `specificMaterials` pair had two fields feeding one selector with the combining rule unstated; `flowSuppliesMaterial` ORed them while the type's own JSDoc claimed the id list narrowed the tag, so the list could only widen and 2GN.78's three re-keyed flows silently reached the whole class. Making it narrow would have expressed 'no metals except gold' but not 'all metals except gold' (only by enumerating the complement, which freezes against a growing catalogue); a single explicit material list had the same gap and also lost the open-over-the-catalogue property of a class tag. Selector arms are tagged because `bone`, `glass` and `leather` each name both a `MaterialTag` and a material id. **Scope addition:** `MaterialName` (`types/tags.ts`) now types every material id — `MaterialDefinition.id`, `RegionalAvailability.materialId`, `GeologicalContext.materialAvailability`'s key, `MaterialAssignment.materialId` and the selector's `id` arm — declared rather than derived from `MATERIALS` (the import would cycle) and pinned to the catalogue by a two-directional test. Doc 05 §3.4 and doc 12 §2.41 record it

Every other pair is byte-identical; all 30 calibration pins hold with nothing re-recorded; 578 tests pass. Two deliberate `as MaterialName` casts remain in `decoration.test.ts`, exercising the runtime unknown-id guard that the type now makes unreachable through normal call sites — still worth keeping against a persisted save or a future catalogue edit. Follow-on left open: whether `excludes` should ever carry a `{ tag }` arm in authored data (it is typed for it, for disambiguation rather than expressiveness, and no shipped flow uses one).

tasks.description: **RULED 2026-08-12 (PR #57 review), implemented same branch.** Give `ClassificationRule` a stable `id` so a rule has an identity independent of its position. An id-based reference cannot go quietly stale: `requireRuleById` throws naming the missing id, verified by deleting a rule and watching the suite fail. **Scope:** `R{n}` survives as a display label only. Dated measurement records (`calibration.test.ts`'s fire-rate tables, doc 12, the spikes) keep their original numbering, since they describe the 44-rule set as measured; only live cross-references were migrated.

tasks.description: design spike — what defines an artefact's working end in general, for artefacts with no edge? 2GN.108 ruled that normalisation must orient the artefact (working end at a shared pole across all artefacts sharing a dimensional axis) and that orientation is achieved by reversal rather than rejection, but ruled the general pole definition out of its own scope. For edged forms the working end is the edge; for a hafted head it is the head; for a vessel, disc, ring or pin there may be no functional pole at all. Rule whether orientation is total (every artefact oriented, which needs a pole rule for shapes that have no working end) or partial by design (only artefacts with a distinguishable functional pole are oriented, the rest left unoriented as `bladeLengthBand` already reports `'none'` for edgeless forms). ⚠️ this blocks implementation rather than 2GN.108's ruling: reversal cannot be implemented for edged forms and retrofitted to a different general convention without repeating the recalibration sweep
tasks.notes: Split out of 2GN.108 during the 2026-08-13 spike session. 2GN.108 established that `position` is intended as an oriented shared axis but is minted in `grammar.ts` as a depth-first traversal index (primary-before-attachments), so the invariant is unenforced — a blade can land at position 0 with its haft after it, and nothing rejects or reverses it. The three existing plausibility proxies (`hasGrippableSecondComponent`, `hasAdequateGripLength`, `hasRigidShaft`) each guess around this absence. Reversal was chosen over rejection because a mirrored artefact carries no information (it is the same artefact described backwards), so rejecting it spends re-expansion budget to enforce something probabilistically rather than by construction — but reversal only works if orientation is definable wherever it is applied, which is this spike's question. ⚠️ **Constraint added 2026-08-13 by 2GN.118 (Finding 6):** `bar-form`'s `taper: ['none','single-end','both-ends']` encodes *which end*, and `single-end` is not reversal-invariant — reverse the component and it still reads 'one end' while which end has silently changed, with no data recording which it was. `none` and `both-ends` are symmetric and survive reversal untouched; `single-end` is the sole asymmetric value in the parameter. No classification rule reads `single-end` — `hasImpactSurfaceIn` tests `bar-form`'s taper only for `'none'`, and the one other rule-side consumer (`bladeProfile`, `classification.ts:181`) reads `elongated`'s taper, a different primitive whose `['none','gradual','abrupt']` vocabulary is symmetric and reversal-safe. The description layer does read it, though: `data/descriptions/observational/bar-form.ts:43` interpolates it into 'The form narrows with a `#taper#` taper.' (asserted at `prose.test.ts:123`), so `single-end` already reaches player-facing prose. A reversal would therefore leave a description asserting which end tapers while no data records which end it was — doc 02 pillar 3 (Simulation Honesty), not a dormant parameter — so whatever this spike rules must either make `single-end` a claim about the oriented axis or accept that reversal silently corrupts it. Ruling reversal without addressing it leaves a parameter whose meaning depends on a traversal order the ruling is designed to stop being meaningful.

tasks.description: design spike — should component roles (grip-system, head-system and whatever else the vocabulary needs) become first-class grammar output? All three rules in `data/plausibility.ts` are explicitly proxies standing in for an absent role concept: `hasGrippableSecondComponent` merely counts components, `hasAdequateGripLength` looks for some other medium/long `bar-form` or `elongated` component anywhere on the artefact (its own comment conceding a `disc-form` elsewhere "says nothing about grip length"), and `hasRigidShaft` accepts any rigid `sheet-form`/`bar-form` regardless of whether it bears the load. `types/plausibility.ts` names the same hole: the model cannot express a property-level concept like "a grippable component". Rule whether roles are authored into the grammar, derived from the attachment graph, or left as proxies for MVP — and if authored, what the role vocabulary is and what it costs across the primitive registry

tasks.description: design spike — are the primitive grammar's categorical parameter value-sets rational and justified? `PRIMITIVE_PARAMETERS` (`data/grammars/primitives.ts`) reproduces doc 05 §5.3 verbatim, so this audits the spec's own vocabularies rather than any code drift. Surfaced by 2GN.97 2026-08-13 while stress-testing whether `baseType` is a genuine categorical: it is, but the value-sets around it are not obviously deliberate. Three measured instances, all of the same shape — two primitives expressing the same concept with disjoint vocabularies, so a value is unreachable by primitive type rather than by design. (a) `base`: `cylindrical` rolls `['flat','rounded','pointed']`, `hollow-enclosed` rolls `['flat','rounded','pedestal']`, making a pedestalled bowl and a pointed cylinder both unreachable — and capping `base-pedestal-display`'s population at hollow-enclosed containers. (b) `opening`: `cylindrical` rolls `['open','restricted','closed']` while `hollow-enclosed` rolls `['wide','narrow','slit','none']` — different vocabularies AND different arities for one concept, leaving `slit` (read by `container-slit-votive`) unreachable on cylinders. (c) `perforation`: `flat-broad` rolls `['none','single','multiple']`, `disc-form` rolls `['none','central','off-centre']` — disjoint, so `perforation-central-rotation` can only ever fire on discs and `perforation-single-pendant` only on flat-broads. Rule for each parameter whether the split is deliberate morphological modelling or an artefact of authoring the BNF primitive-by-primitive; where deliberate, record why; where not, rule the corrected vocabulary. Same shape as 2GN.87's reachability finding, applied to the grammar's inputs rather than a rule's condition
tasks.notes: Filed 2026-08-13 from the 2GN.97 spike session, which reached it by stress-testing whether `baseType` is a genuine categorical (it is — unlike `wallThickness`, there is no crushed continuous quantity beneath it). The audit question is one level up: whether the value-sets themselves were designed or accreted. ⚠️ Ruling here may change which values exist, so anything authoring rules against them or deriving from them waits: 2GN.10 (`allowedMaterialTags` from primitive type + properties), 2GN.21 (`physicalLabel` from these observable values), 2GN.109 (replacement edge-family rule) and 2GN.117 (re-bands `bladeLengthBand` off `elongated.length`). 2GN.97 is NOT a dependent — it surfaced the defect rather than consuming the vocabulary. **Ruled 2026-08-13 — see docs/spikes/2GN.118-primitive-parameter-value-sets.md.** Seven disjoint shared-name pairs found, not the three filed. `base` unions to `[flat, rounded, pointed, pedestal]` on both primitives (the split made `base-pointed-amphora` unfireable on anything amphora-shaped, since `dominantContainer` always prefers `hollow-enclosed`); `diameter` unifies to `small/medium/large` with derivation owned by 2GN.120; `crossSection`, `shape` and `taper` stay as authored, being genuine per-primitive geometry; `opening` and `perforation` are deferred whole to 2GN.122, each being two axes crushed into one field rather than a vocabulary split. The two base rules keep their weights (authored in cb3e517 before EXPECTED_FIRE_RATES existed, so never fitted to observed rates); only the fire rates move. Ships no src/ change: each ruling lands in its own task so EXPECTED_FIRE_RATES re-records once. Per-culture base weighting filed as 2GN.121; taper reversal constraint recorded on 2GN.115.

tasks.description: design spike — should classification conditions read *relations between components* rather than isolated component properties? Measured 2026-08-13 over all 43 shipped rules during 2GN.97: **10 of the 24 unmigrated rules condition on exactly one property** (`f.x === 'value'` and nothing else) — `base-pedestal-display`, `base-pointed-amphora`, the three `perforation-*` rules, both `ring-*` rules, both `sheet-*` rules and `size-small-personal`. A further 7 read two properties that both describe the *same* component (the container rules pair `hasContainer`, a presence flag, with a feature extracted off the dominant container). Exactly one rule is genuinely relational (`motif-multiple-origins`, comparing origins across the artefact's decoration). A base is a relationship between the base and what it supports: a pedestal under a statue and a pedestal under a hat-stand carry opposite readings, identical `baseType`, and no amount of culture-relativity separates them because the difference is not cultural. The rule reads one term of a two-term relation and discards the term carrying the meaning — doc 02 Simulation Honesty. ⚠️ This is orthogonal to doc 11 §2.9's absolute/relative cut: `perforation-central-rotation` awards `tool` (an AbsoluteTag) and is under-conditioned identically, so the defect is a property of how conditions are written, not of which vocabulary they award from. `NormalisedArtefact.attachments` and `NormalisedComponent.position` are populated and unread by every rule — the same unused-graph finding as 2GN.108. Rule whether conditions gain access to component relations, what that does to `ClassificationRule.condition`'s signature (already widened once by 2GN.80), and which rules are rewritten versus left as affordance readings
tasks.notes: Filed 2026-08-13 from the 2GN.97 spike session. Scope is **all 43 rules**, not the 24 unmigrated ones: the measurement that produced it covered the 24, but the defect cuts across the absolute/relative boundary, so scoping to relative-award rules would audit the wrong set. Supersedes the framing 2GN.97 inherited — those rules are not unmigrated-but-fine awaiting a baseline, a class of them is under-conditioned, and no baseline of any kind fixes an under-conditioned rule. Absorbs the ambiguity originally filed as a competing-readings question (a central perforation reads spindle-whorl or pendant depending on the disc's size, mass and what it attaches to — the ambiguity IS the missing relational term). ⚠️ Interacts with 2GN.118: that audits which parameter *values* exist, this audits what a condition may *read*. Independent questions on the same surface; neither blocks the other.

tasks.description: `engine/generation/grammar.ts` — derive `wallThickness` as a modelled quantity rather than a free three-value roll. Today `PRIMITIVE_PARAMETERS` rolls `wall: ['thin','medium','thick']` directly, with no continuous value beneath and no input from craft process, material or vessel role. Three consequences ruled in 2GN.97 (2026-08-13): (a) thickness is plausibly a *derivative of the crafting process* and is currently uninfluenced by `craftSpecialisation`, the component's assigned material or what the vessel is for; (b) three rungs is the entire gradation available, too coarse for the distinctions the classification rules try to draw on it; (c) **cross-culture comparison is impossible by construction** — one culture's `thick` may be physically thinner than another's `thin`, and since the band is cut from a global table before anything culture-relative is consulted, no baseline can recover the difference. Fourth instance of the band-computed-from-an-absolute-table family after 2GN.86 (mass), 2GN.87 (blade) and 2GN.108 (axis). Deliverable: a derived thickness quantity with its inputs ruled, and bands cut per-culture rather than globally. ⚠️ **Scope extended 2026-08-13 by 2GN.118 (Finding 5):** `diameter` joins this task as the same defect in a second parameter. 2GN.118 unified its labels (`cylindrical`’s `narrow/medium/wide` and `ring-form`/`disc-form`’s `small/medium/large` were one three-rung axis under two names) but ruled the derivation here, because the argument for keeping the two label sets apart is really an argument for deriving: a cylinder’s diameter reads relative to its own length (a wide tube is wide *for a tube*) whereas a disc’s diameter is its principal dimension, which is a ratio to model rather than two vocabularies to maintain. Nothing reads `diameter` today, so it carries no live consequence yet — but 2GN.118 noted that “harmless because unread” is exactly what let `base-pointed-amphora` sit broken.
tasks.notes: Filed 2026-08-13 by the 2GN.97 ruling, which found `vessel-thin-walled-fine-ware` and `vessel-thick-walled-utilitarian` unrelativisable: no baseline of any kind — prevalence, stratification or weight-scaling — can relativise a three-value label rolled from a global table, because there is no quantity for a culture to have opinions about. Prevalence in particular cannot work here (unlike `baseType`, where it can): band frequency says nothing about actual thickness, so a culture whose walls are all 3mm and one whose walls are all 30mm both read '100% thin' or '100% thick' depending only on where the global cut falls. ⚠️ The two wall rules stay as they are until this lands — they were left absolute rather than migrated or deleted, recorded as blocked-with-reason. ⚠️ Overlaps 2GN.118, which audits whether the `wall` vocabulary is justified at all; if that spike rules the three-value set out, this task's shape changes with it.

tasks.description: design spike — is there one aperture model, and does it subsume `perforation`? 2GN.118 ruled (2026-08-13) that `opening` is not one axis but at least two crushed into one field: **presence/count** (`closed`/`none` are the same physical fact, scored identically at 0 by `OPENNESS_BY_OPENING`) and **aperture size** (`wide`/`narrow`/`slit`). It also ruled the `cylindrical`/`hollow-enclosed` vocabularies commensurable — `OPENNESS_BY_OPENING` already ranks all seven values on one 0–1 scale, and three shipped rules (`container-wide-open`, `container-restricted-access`, `container-closed-sealed`) pair the cylinder and vessel labels as synonyms by hand, which is the rule layer compensating for a split that should not exist. Two questions this spike owns. **(1) Multiplicity**: a through-void has two mouths (bead, socketed axe, tube) and a two-mouthed vase has two separate apertures — these are different facts and neither is expressible today. **(2) Subsumption**: a hole through a disc (`perforation`) and a hole through a cylinder wall (`opening`) are plausibly one concept split across two parameter names by primitive-by-primitive BNF authoring, the same defect as `base` one level up. If they are one axis, `perforation`'s count/position split (2GN.118's case (c), deferred here whole rather than ruled) resolves inside this model instead. Rule the axis set (count, size, through/blind, position), which parameters survive, and what `ExtractedFeatures` carries. ⚠️ 8 shipped rules read `openingType` or `perforation`; `EXPECTED_FIRE_RATES` re-records once at implementation, which is why this is ruled before 2GN.118's own vocabulary changes are implemented rather than after
tasks.notes: Filed 2026-08-13 from the 2GN.118 spike session, cases (b) `opening` and (c) `perforation`. The full cross-tabulation of `PRIMITIVE_PARAMETERS` found seven disjoint shared-name pairs, not the three originally filed: `base`, `opening`, `perforation` (all unioned into `ExtractedFeatures` and read by rules) plus `crossSection`, `diameter`, `shape`, `taper` (read by no rule, so no live consequence). 2GN.118 ruled on `base` and on the four unread pairs; `opening` and `perforation` were split out here because they outgrew a vocabulary fix. `opening` is the worst of the three splits — zero shared values between the two primitives AND different arities (3 vs 4) for one concept — but the fix is not a union: Jason ruled the two-axis reading, and then raised multiplicity, which neither vocabulary can express at any arity. Subsumption is this spike's open question and was deliberately not ruled in 2GN.118 for want of measurement: if `opening` and `perforation` are one aperture axis, ruling `opening` first and merging `perforation` later means recalibrating `EXPECTED_FIRE_RATES` twice. Scoped as one spike rather than two on that basis. Renaming was considered and rejected as a separate concern: splitting the axes makes the intuitive vocabulary fall out (`closed`/`none` → count, `open` → `wide`, `restricted` → `narrow`), so no new words are needed for the values that survive.

tasks.description: `types/world.ts` + `engine/generation/materials.ts` + `engine/generation/decoration.ts` — re-key `CulturalProfile.materialAffinities` from `Map<MaterialTag, number>` to the `MaterialSelector` tagged union 2GN.112 built for `MaterialFlow`, resolved **most-specific-wins**. 2GN.110 ruled this on 2026-08-13 and nothing has carried it: the type is still tag-keyed at `types/world.ts:220`, and `data/explorer-cultures.ts` still holds the comment recording Thalassar’s dropped `precious-metal: 1.2` as an open design question. A bare `MaterialTag | MaterialName` union cannot work because `bone`, `glass` and `leather` each name both a class and a material, which is exactly why the flow side needed the tagged form. `includes`/`excludes` does NOT transfer: membership needs subtraction, affinities are weights with nothing to subtract. tasks.notes: Filed 2026-08-13 during PR #61 review. 2GN.110 was marked done on the strength of its ruling, but no task carried the implementation: `2GN.27`, `2GN.68`, `2GN.114` and `3WS.3` all depend on 2GN.110 while consuming or fixture-building around affinities rather than re-keying them, so the ruling had no destination. Surfaced by a review comment on `site/design/classification.html`, which described the new shape as shipped when the type had not moved; the page now describes it as a ruled contract, and this task is what makes it true. Product-of-deviations was rejected in the ruling (1.5 × 0.8 = 1.2, so a below-neutral authored value would yield an above-neutral weight). A specific entry with no class entry is well-formed and is the case that recovers Thalassar exactly.

tasks.description: `src/lib/data/materials.ts` + `src/lib/types/tags.ts` — widen the material catalogue beyond the 16 shipped materials, scoped to what artefact generation and craft actually need. Four of the eight `MaterialTag` classes are single-leaf (clay, glass, fiber, leather), so `materials.calibration.test.ts` emits no intra-tag split for them — it would "always read 100% and carry no information" — leaving half the guard's two-level tree unmeasurable by construction. Covers both filling out thin classes (copper, tin and lead under `metal`; wool and hemp under `fiber`; further clays) and breadth for archaeological plausibility (shell, amber, horn, pigments, composite materials), judged by what a real assemblage needs rather than by filling tag rows for their own sake. ⚠️ may require new `MaterialTag` members, which touches the `MaterialSelector` keyspace and every authored `materialAffinities` entry array; `MATERIAL_NAMES` is declared rather than derived from `MATERIALS` (the import would cycle), so `materials.test.ts`'s two-directional pin fails loudly until the list is updated alongside. ⚠️ moves material-share distributions, so `EXPECTED_TAG_SHARES` and `EXPECTED_INTRA_TAG_SHARES` need re-recording
tasks.notes: ⚠️ **Forward hazard (2GN.128, 2026-08-14):** this task changes the availability model the affinity-silence validator computes its verdict from, so materials that were legitimately silent may become accessible and re-open violations 2GN.128 closed. Re-run the validator and re-close the four presets as part of this task.

tasks.description: design spike — does `AvailabilityLevel` conflate materials that are **found** with materials that are **produced**? `GeologicalContext`'s own JSDoc calls itself "geological material scarcity" and cites obsidian, gold and tin, yet it keys `leather`, `linen`, `bone`, `antler`, `oak`, `ash`, `fired-clay` and `glass` — none of which are geological. Measured 2026-08-13: **10 of the 16 shipped materials are produced rather than dug.** Sharpest are `bronze` and `iron`: bronze does not exist in the ground at all (an alloy requiring tin *and* copper) and iron requires smelting from ore, yet each carries a single `AvailabilityLevel` conflating "the ore is here" with "we can smelt it". **This double-counts**, because `computeMaterialWeight` multiplies `scarcityWeight × phaseTechnologyWeight` as independent terms: for granite they genuinely are independent (the rock is underfoot; carving is a separate skill), but Tarpan's bronze `scarce` stands in for ore-plus-tin-plus-smelting, which its `metallurgy: 0.6` already encodes — the same constraint applied twice. It also makes authoring unstatable: nothing can express "abundant cattle, no tanning tradition" or "rich ore, no smelting" as distinct from simply "little leather" or "little iron". Rule whether `AvailabilityLevel` splits into substrate-versus-product, whether a `requiresExtraction` flag or an input-material relation hangs off `MaterialDefinition`, or whether `craftDomain` absorbs the distinction. Sequenced after 2GN.124 deliberately, so the ruling is made against the widened catalogue rather than a 16-material sample that may not contain the awkward cases
tasks.notes: Filed 2026-08-13 from a preset-cultures audit. The conflation surfaced while checking whether each preset's authored affinities were reachable: Tarpan authors `metal: 1.3` and its geology marks bronze `scarce`, which reads as a statement about deposits but is really a statement about metallurgy. Downstream of 2GN.124 because the ruling should be made against the full catalogue — a widened `metal` class carrying copper and tin separately may itself resolve part of the bronze case, and ruling first would risk modelling around a gap the catalogue task closes.

All three already sit behind the M2 gate via 3WS.1, so these edges record ordering rather than changing any status today — they survive the gate lifting, which is the point. ⚠️ **Forward hazard (2GN.128, 2026-08-14):** this task changes the availability model the affinity-silence validator computes its verdict from, so materials that were legitimately silent may become accessible and re-open violations 2GN.128 closed. Re-run the validator and re-close the four presets as part of this task.

tasks.description: design spike — should a material absent from `CulturalProfile.materialAffinities` resolve to the neutral `1`, or is silence an authoring error that should throw? `culturalAffinityWeight` (`engine/generation/materials.ts`) returns `1` for any material no entry matches, and `computeTechniqueWeight` (`decoration.ts`) does the same for `techniqueAffinities` — so **an unauthored material is indistinguishable from one deliberately authored at exactly `1.0`.** Measured 2026-08-13 across the four Explorer presets: 8–12 of 16 materials and 13–14 of 16 techniques resolve by default rather than by authorship, so most of every preset is silence. Xoconahtl's `['clay', 1.0]` is the case that exposes it — behaviourally identical to omitting the entry, kept only because a comment says it is deliberate indifference, which is exactly the distinction the type cannot carry. ⚠️ The stakes cut both ways and the spike must weigh both: throwing makes every preset state a judgement about every material (~250 authored numbers across four presets today, growing with 2GN.124's widened catalogue) and turns a new material into a breaking change for all authored cultures; keeping the default leaves "considered and indifferent" and "never considered" permanently indistinguishable, which is the same silently-dead-authoring failure 2GN.84 measured on the retired `precious-*` entries. Options to rule between include: keep the default; throw on omission; require an explicit neutral sentinel; or a `completeness: 'partial' | 'exhaustive'` flag on the profile letting a culture opt into strictness. Applies equally to `techniqueAffinities`, `contextWeights` and `siteTypeWeights`, which share the shape — rule the family, not the one map
tasks.notes: Filed 2026-08-13 from a preset-cultures audit. Sits alongside doc 12 §2.47's lesson that a dormant path accumulates no evidence about itself: a defaulted entry is dormant authoring, and nothing in the suite can tell it from a decision. Related to 2GN.124 (a widened catalogue multiplies the authoring cost of throwing) but not blocked on it — the ruling is about the contract, not the catalogue size, and can be made against the 16 shipped materials. Ruled 2026-08-14 — see docs/spikes/2GN.127-affinity-silence.md, doc 11 §2.15 and doc 12 §2.49. **Silence is legitimate iff the material is inaccessible** (`absent` locally with no flow reaching it, or unmodelled in that geology); anything obtainable locally or by trade must carry an entry, class or specific, enforced by a validator at profile-construction time. None of the four options in the brief was taken: absence is derivable from `isAvailable`, so the distinction becomes a validation question rather than a syntax one — no sentinel, no completeness flag, no migration of authored profiles. ⚠️ Throwing on all omission was rejected for abolishing absence rather than distinguishing it. Two corrections to the brief: `contextWeights`/`siteTypeWeights` have **no engine readers**, so ruling the whole family would author contracts against unobserved behaviour; and `isAvailable`'s MVP lenience reads unmodelled as available, which inverts the rule, so the validator treats it as a third state. Measured 31 violations against 8 legitimate silences across the four presets. Implementation is 2GN.128; `techniqueAffinities` is 2GN.129, deferred behind the `materialAccessGate` `> 1` substrate-gate defect the ruling surfaced.

tasks.description: `engine/generation/cultureValidation.ts` (new) + `data/explorer-cultures.ts` — enforce the 2GN.127 ruling: silence in `CulturalProfile.materialAffinities` is legitimate **iff** the material is inaccessible to that culture (`absent` locally with no `MaterialFlow` reaching it, **or** unmodelled in that geology); a material that is locally obtainable, or `trade-only` with a flow that reaches it, must carry a matching entry, class or specific. Validator throws at profile-construction time, not during generation. ⚠️ `isAvailable`'s MVP lenience returns `true` for an unmodelled material, which read naively inverts the rule — unmodelled is the strongest case for "never encountered", so the validator must treat `level === undefined` as a third state, the way `scarcityWeight`'s JSDoc already does, rather than folding it into accessible. ⚠️ The obligation is **one-directional**: accessible ⟹ must be covered; covered ⟹ nothing implied about access, so an entry covering an inaccessible material is legal and silent. Class entries discharge the obligation (most-specific-wins already treats a `{ tag }` entry as each covered material's real weight), which is what keeps authoring terse — khaltiris states 2 entries covering 8 materials. Measured 2026-08-14 across the four presets: **31 violations against 8 legitimate silences** (tarpan 6/3, thalassar 11/1, xoconahtl 6/4, khaltiris 8/0), so all four are re-authored here and the validator throws from the start. Khaltiris has no legitimate silences and must state a position on all 16 materials. Presets are re-authored to fit the rule, not the reverse: they exist to showcase the engine. Xoconahtl's `['clay', 1.0]` and its comment naming this question resolve here
tasks.notes: Ruled by 2GN.127 on 2026-08-14 — see docs/spikes/2GN.127-affinity-silence.md, doc 11 §2.15 and doc 12 §2.49. Ships ahead of 2GN.124/2GN.126 deliberately: both rewrite the availability model the validator reads, so each will re-open violations this task closes, but the validator is the durable artefact and building it first is what makes those tasks' preset edits checkable. ⚠️ Forward hazard recorded on 2GN.124 and 2GN.126. Scope is `materialAffinities` only — `techniqueAffinities` is 2GN.129, and `contextWeights`/`siteTypeWeights` have no engine readers at all and inherit the principle when they get one (ruling strictness for a dormant map is the defect 2GN.87 punished). **Landed 2026-08-14** — validator is `findAffinitySilenceViolations` / `assertAffinitiesCoverAccessibleMaterials` in `engine/generation/cultureValidation.ts`; enforcement point is module load in `data/explorer-cultures.ts`. All 31 violations closed (tarpan 7 entries, thalassar 12, xoconahtl 8, khaltiris 9); suite 594 → 611 passing with no calibration pin re-recorded. Two findings recorded in doc 12 §2.50: the three-state read needed no new export (`explainMaterialWeight` already returns `level` and `available` separately, so accessibility is `level !== undefined && available`, and the private region helpers stayed private); and a duplicate class selector silently voids `materials.calibration.test.ts`'s `classLifted` arm, which is why thalassar discharges bronze/iron specifically rather than with a `metal` class entry. Xoconahtl's `['clay', 1.0]` keeps its value — only the comment was discharged — because it is the live instance of the `> 1` substrate-gate defect 2GN.129 rules.

tasks.description: `engine/generation/decoration.ts` — extend the 2GN.127 silence rule to `techniqueAffinities`, and rule the substrate-gate question it exposes. Techniques have a derivable accessibility one hop out: `materialAccessGate` already establishes that a culture with no gold cannot gild and no engravable material cannot engrave, so "silence is legitimate iff inaccessible" transposes cleanly. ⚠️ **Blocked on a prior defect, which is this task's to rule**: `materialAccessGate`'s substrate check requires `culturalAffinityWeight(material, culture) > 1`, strictly better than neutral, so a material authored at exactly `1.0` fails it identically to one the culture cannot obtain. Once 2GN.128 pushes cultures to author far more entries, a culture that explicitly states indifference to bronze gets bronze-substrate techniques suppressed exactly as though bronze were unobtainable — the ambivalent-versus-absent collapse 2GN.127 exists to eliminate, reappearing inside the gate meant to model access. Whether affinity should gate substrate access at all is the question; `hasIntroducedMaterialAccess` deliberately gates on availability alone and is the contrast case. ⚠️ moves technique-selection distributions, so decorative calibration guards need re-recording with the drift annotated ⚠️ Measured 2026-08-14 by 2GN.128 and now live in the presets: xoconahtl authors `['clay', 1.0]` against `abundant` clay, and it fails the gate (`affinity=1, isAvailable=true` → substrate access `false`). 2GN.128 deliberately kept the `1.0` rather than nudging it past the gate, so the evidence survives for this ruling.

tasks.description: `src/lib/data/names/modern.ts` — the curated modern language: one pinned `Phonology` shared by every world seed, naming the player's own institutions, venues and colleagues. Generated by `generatePhonology` from a fixed seed constant rather than hand-authored, so it emanates from the same system as the ancient languages and inherits any later sound-change work; curated only in the sense that its seed is pinned, not rolled per world. Establishes the diegetic contrast the interpretive frame needs: the player reads ancient names *through* a modern tongue, and the untranslated-tablet phase later depends on the player's own language being a fixed, known reference point against which unknown ones are strange. Adds a `MODERN_LANGUAGE_ID` reserved outside the per-world `LanguageForest`, since it belongs to no ancient family and must never be assigned to a culture.
tasks.notes: Ruled during the 2GN.66 spike conversation: the modern language sits OUTSIDE `LanguageForest`, not as a family of one inside it. The forest is per-world-seed and generated; this is global and fixed, so a member inside it would be a language belonging to no culture. `generatePhonology(createPrng(MODERN_LANGUAGE_SEED))` is the whole curation mechanism — a fixed seed string yields one stable phonology, verified during 2GN.66.

Rule the input set and the weighting shape, then thread it through `expandGrammar`'s determinism-critical draw sequence. ⚠️ moves `base-pedestal-display` and `base-pointed-amphora` fire rates, so `EXPECTED_FIRE_RATES` needs re-recording with the drift annotated
tasks.notes: Filed 2026-08-13 from the 2GN.118 spike session, case (a) `base`. The spike measured that `cylindrical` rolled `['flat','rounded','pointed']` and `hollow-enclosed` rolled `['flat','rounded','pedestal']`, making a pedestalled cylinder and a pointed vessel unreachable by primitive type rather than by design — and, because `dominantContainer` (`engine/generation/classification.ts`) always prefers `hollow-enclosed` over `cylindrical`, `base-pointed-amphora` could only ever fire on cylinder-dominant artefacts (sockets, ferrules), never on anything amphora-shaped. Jason ruled the extractor's primitive-type branch stays in place as a marked seam rather than collapsing to a single `bandProp` call, on the grounds that the codebase trends toward greater granularity and per-culture divergence is wanted: the branch cannot express a frequency difference (only impossible vs equally-likely), so the divergence has to return as weights, and this task owns that.
